title: Manyikeni
description: A stone-walled settlement in the style of Great Zimbabwe is built near the coast, linking the plateau to Indian Ocean trade.

title: Vasco da Gama reaches Mozambique Island
description: The Portuguese fleet on its way to India calls at a Swahili trading town whose sultan's name is later given to the whole country.

title: Portuguese fort at Sofala
description: Pêro de Anaia builds a fort at the port through which the gold of the interior reaches the coast.

title: Portuguese settle Mozambique Island
description: The Portuguese establish a port and naval base that serves as the capital of their East African possessions for almost four centuries.

title: Lourenço Marques explores Delagoa Bay
description: A Portuguese trader explores the bay on which the future capital will stand.

title: Separate government for Mozambique
description: The colony, until then ruled from Goa, receives its own governor.

title: Gaza Empire founded
description: The Nguni leader Soshangane, driven north by the wars of Shaka, builds a kingdom that comes to rule most of southern Mozambique.

title: Delagoa Bay awarded to Portugal
description: The French president, acting as arbitrator, rejects the British claim to the bay.

title: Mozambique Company chartered
description: Portugal hands the centre of the colony to a chartered company, largely financed from abroad, which governs it until 1942.

title: Capture of Gungunhana
description: Portuguese troops under Mouzinho de Albuquerque seize the last ruler of Gaza, ending the largest independent state in the colony.

title: Battle of Ngomano
description: The German force of Lettow-Vorbeck crosses from German East Africa, routs a Portuguese garrison and campaigns in the colony for most of a year.

title: Mueda massacre
description: Portuguese troops fire on Makonde demonstrators, an event that turns many towards armed resistance.

title: FRELIMO founded
description: Exiled nationalist groups unite in the Mozambique Liberation Front under Eduardo Mondlane.

title: War of independence begins
description: FRELIMO guerrillas attack a Portuguese post, opening ten years of war.

title: Wiriyamu massacre
description: Portuguese troops kill several hundred villagers, and reports of it abroad damage support for the colonial war.

title: Lusaka Accord
description: Portugal's new government agrees with FRELIMO on a ceasefire and a transfer of power.

title: Independence
description: Mozambique becomes independent as a one-party state under Samora Machel.

title: Nkomati Accord
description: Mozambique and South Africa each promise to stop supporting the other's armed opponents, though South African aid to RENAMO continues.

title: Death of Samora Machel
description: The president's aircraft crashes just inside South Africa, and Joaquim Chissano succeeds him.

title: Rome peace accords
description: The government and RENAMO end a fifteen-year civil war in which about a million people died.

title: First multiparty election
description: FRELIMO and Joaquim Chissano win a vote in which RENAMO takes part as a political party.

title: Floods
description: Weeks of rain and a cyclone flood the southern river valleys, killing about 700 people and displacing hundreds of thousands.

title: Insurgency in Cabo Delgado begins
description: Armed Islamists attack police stations in a northern port, the start of a conflict that displaces hundreds of thousands.

title: Cyclone Idai
description: One of the worst storms recorded in the southern hemisphere wrecks Beira and floods central Mozambique, killing more than 600 people in the country.
